We will prove this by verifying hypotheses (a), (b), and (c) of
Lemma <REF_0001>.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Since <MATH_0001> is locally free over <MATH_0002>
we see that we have short exact sequences
<MATH_0003>
for all <MATH_0004>. Thus condition (b) holds by
Cohomology, Lemma <REF_0002>.

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
As <MATH_0005> is a nonzerodivisor we obtain short exact sequences
<MATH_0006>
and we have corresponding short exact sequences
<MATH_0007>.
We will use
Local Cohomology, Lemma
<REF_0003>
without further mention. Our assumptions imply that
<MATH_0008> and
<MATH_0009>
are finite <MATH_0010>-modules. Hence the same thing is true for <MATH_0011>, see
Local Cohomology, Lemma
<REF_0004>.
Using induction and the short exact sequences we find that
<MATH_0012> are finite <MATH_0013>-modules for all <MATH_0014>.
In this way we see hypothesis (c) is satisfied.

<STRUCT_0005><STRUCT_0006>
Finally, as <MATH_0015> is a finite <MATH_0016>-module
we can apply Cohomology, Lemma <REF_0005>
to see hypothesis (a) holds.

In Lemma <REF_0001>
if <MATH_0001> is universally catenary with Cohen-Macaulay
formal fibres (for example if <MATH_0002> has a dualizing complex), then
the condition that
<MATH_0003> and <MATH_0004>
are finite <MATH_0005>-modules, is equivalent with
<MATH_0006>
for all <MATH_0007>
and <MATH_0008>
by Local Cohomology, Theorem <REF_0002>.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
For example, if <MATH_0009> is <MATH_0010> and if every irreducible
component of <MATH_0011> has codimension <MATH_0012>
in <MATH_0013>, then we get the finiteness of
<MATH_0014> and <MATH_0015>.
This should be contrasted with the slightly weaker conditions
found in Lemma <REF_0003>
(see also Remark <REF_0004>).
